Subject: Territorial commitments — kickoff and questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the overview last week. As we kick off the technical review with our privacy ops and cloud teams, a few practical questions have come up that we need clarified before we proceed with the DPA addendum:

1) Can Redwood commit to a per-tenant region affinity for production inference (EU-only for our EU customers) with a documented transient failover window and the maximum duration for ephemeral cross-border processing?

2) If short-window cross-region processing occurs (for failover, warmup, or batch rehydration), what telemetry do you capture and retain that proves country/region of execution per request? We need a footprint for audit evidence.

3) Please send your current subprocessor roster (including cloud infra partners and any third-party inference accelerators) and call out which subprocessors may cause data to transit outside the EU even for short windows.

We'd like the roster and a short one-page summary of the territorial commitment (maximum failover window, retention of region-evidence logs, and KMS locality guarantees) by EOD Wednesday so our legal and infra teams can open a path to the DPA addendum review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — hoping to get this into our June procurement sprint.

Best,
Sandra Perez
Data Protection Officer
MedAlign Health

--
MedAlign Health | Confidential

Sandra — thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Marissa (CS lead), Jonas (inference ops), and Laura (legal) to make sure we cover the technical, operational, and contractual angles.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can offer tenant-level region affinity in our Private and Dedicated offerings; for Hosted we provide region affinity by account with an operationally documented failover policy.
- Transient cross-region processing is limited to a configurable failover window; our current recommendation for EU-only customers is a 72-hour bounded window for warmup/failover operations unless an extended incident requires an exception and documented approval.
- We capture per-request execution region tags plus trace spans and a minimal execution manifest (node id, region, approximate timestamp). Logs are retained per our audit retention policy; we'll include the exact retention durations and sampling rates in the summary.

I'll attach the subprocessor roster and a one-page commitment summary for you. Laura will propose contract language for the DPA addendum and Marissa will coordinate the operational runbook. If this looks good, we can schedule a 45-minute technical walk-through Wed morning (CEST).

Attachments: Redwood_Subprocessor_Roster_2027-06.xlsx; Territorial_Commitment_Summary_v1.pdf; DPA_Addendum_Draft_MedAlign.pdf (draft)

Next step: can you confirm whether MedAlign requires a hard-coded tenancy placement (no cross-region ever), or if the bounded 72h window is acceptable as a policy term?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
From: Sandra Perez <sandra.perez@medalign.com>

Markus — thanks, that was fast. We reviewed the attachments with infra and legal this morning. A few clarifications:

- The 72-hour bounded window is acceptable as a starting point for our procurement team, provided it is coupled with an automatic notification to our ops inbox and a mandatory post-incident report whenever any cross-region processing occurs.
- For telemetry we need mapping to ISO country codes (not just region names) per request, and retention of raw execution manifests for 24 months for audit purposes. Please confirm that you can provide country-level tags and that these manifests will be exportable as CSV/JSON on request with documented access controls.
- On subprocessors: we need any named accelerator/cloud partner that could initiate an outbound cross-border step to be highlighted in the roster and flagged as 'conditional' with a short description of the triggering condition.

We can live with the 72h operational cap plus the two controls above — automatic notification and a post-incident artifact. If Redwood will accept those controls in the addendum, we can move to sign-off on the DPA addendum and start the contract-stage procurement.

Sandra Perez
DPO, MedAlign Health
From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Territorial commitments — kickoff and questions

Hi Sandra — Laura from Redwood legal here. Appreciate the pragmatic ask. We reviewed your requested controls and propose the following contract language (high-level):

1) Territorial Affinity: Redwood will configure production inference to honor account-level EU affinity. Temporary cross-region execution is permitted only as described below.

2) Conditional transient processing: Cross-region processing is permitted for: (a) failover/resiliency events; (b) short-lived warmup or prefetch tasks to rehydrate caches; (c) scheduled maintenance windows where capacity is otherwise unavailable. Such processing will not exceed 72 hours without explicit written approval.

3) Notification & post-incident artifacts: Redwood will automatically notify the customer's designated ops mailbox within 60 minutes of any cross-region execution for the affected account. A post-incident report including per-request country ISO codes and redacted execution manifests will be delivered within 5 business days. Redwood will retain execution manifests for 24 months and make them available under secure export to the customer's compliance team upon validated request.

4) Subprocessors: Redwood will flag any subprocessor in the roster that may cause conditional outbound transit and provide a short note about the trigger condition and mitigation controls.

We're attaching a draft DPA addendum that reflects the above for redlines. We're happy to accept the 72-hour operational cap + notification + 24-month artifact retention as you requested, subject to the final redline. If that aligns with MedAlign's position, our contracts team can issue the DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Next steps suggested:
- Marissa: schedule the Wed technical walkthrough with MedAlign infra (Jonas to present telemetry and manifests).
- Markus: coordinate timelines for legal/counterparty redlines.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
